Rural California / Wildfire season

Mountain, desert and Central Valley towns often have one wired provider or none. Planned power shutoffs and wildfires can take down any provider—use battery backup and a phone hotspot.

What to verify before choosing an internet plan in California

Provider names on a state guide are a starting point, not confirmation that service reaches every street, apartment or rural address in California. Compare plans using the complete service address and the provider's current offer.

  • Confirm the exact address. Check the house number, apartment or unit, and ZIP code with the provider; nearby homes can have different networks.
  • Compare the real monthly cost. Check how long the promotional rate lasts, the regular rate afterward, equipment rental, installation, taxes, fees and any AutoPay or bundle requirements.
  • Compare performance details. Review upload as well as download speed, data limits, latency where relevant, contract terms and cancellation conditions.
  • Check building access. Renters and condo residents should ask whether the building is wired for the provider and whether installation needs approval.

The FCC National Broadband Map is useful for researching reported coverage, but it is not an order confirmation. Compare national starting-offer examples on our Internet plans page, then use our address availability guide and internet plan total-cost guide. For providers not listed in the national comparison, confirm the current address-specific offer directly with the provider.

Compare internet availability by community in California

Useful local checks: Los Angeles, San Diego, the Bay Area, Sacramento, Fresno, and rural Northern California. These are geographic comparison points, not a claim that any particular provider serves every address in those places.

Separate dense coastal metros from the Central Valley, mountain communities, and rural Northern California. Compare exact addresses in Los Angeles, San Diego, the Bay Area, Sacramento, and Fresno rather than treating statewide provider presence as proof of local service. Enter the complete street address in the availability checker before comparing advertised speeds, introductory prices, equipment charges, data policies, and contract terms. If a provider cannot confirm the address online, ask whether the property is serviceable and whether installation or construction fees apply.

FAQ

Is fiber in Los Angeles and the Bay Area?

In many neighborhoods. AT&T Fiber and Frontier cover parts of Southern California. Test your address.

Best option in rural California?

Start with 5G home if you have signal, then Starlink.
